question.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(2,2)$ where $t=2$, given that $‖{r}^{′}(2)‖=1,$ and the unit tangent vector to the curve is

$$
T(t)=⟨\frac{\sqrt{4t-{t}^{2}}}{2},\,\frac{2-t}{2}⟩.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(2)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(2)=⟨2,2⟩,$ since the point $P(2,2)$ is at the tip of $r(2).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t),$ ${T}^{′}(2)$ and $‖{T}^{′}(2)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{4t-{t}^{2}}}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2-t}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2-t}{2\sqrt{4t-{t}^{2}}},\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(2) & =⟨\frac{2-2}{2\sqrt{4(2)-{2}^{2}}},\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩=⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(2)‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(2) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(2)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(2)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=2$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(2) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(2)}{‖{T}^{′}(2)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})}⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩=⟨0,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2)+R(2)N(2) & =⟨2,2⟩+2⟨0,-1⟩=⟨2,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
